column1: # Plain-language OUTCOME-EXPLANATION realization frames ("Why?" layer) — Reiter &
# Dale (2000) *Building Natural Language Generation Systems* (CUP), the
# realization stage: a communicative goal is realized by filling a STORED
# linguistic template, NOT by concatenating an inline literal in code. These
# frames are the SECOND realization of the same turn — a plain-language gloss of
# WHY the engine produced the outcome it did, sibling of the primary response
# (abstain-frames.tsv / conditional-frames.tsv). Keyed by the existing
# ResponseFrame (pragmatics::response) — no parallel outcome enum — so the "Why?"
# panel and the answer share ONE communicative goal.
# Only the frames whose PRIMARY response does not already carry its own reason
# get a row here. The self-explaining frames (UnprovenRelation, RuleAwaitingFact,
# RuleApplies, RuleDoesNotApply, Comparison, PhaticReturn) get NO row by design:
# their primary surface already states the reason ("I know both X and Y but
# cannot confirm…", "{rule} ({cite}): {text} Whether this applies depends on
# {missing}…"), so realize_why returns None and the renderer shows no Why? panel.
# Each explanation's content is filled from the ACTUAL outcome data of THIS turn
# — the loaded sources reasoned over, the surfaces that did not resolve — never
# from a static description of how the pipeline "works". Plain language, active
# voice, ≤ one idea per sentence (CDC plain-language guidance): abstention is
# designed safety behaviour, stated calmly, never as an error.
# Format: `frame_id<TAB>template`. Typed slots the realizer
# (pragmatics::realize::realize_why) fills, never authored here:
#   {sources}  the plain-language names of the loaded source(s) the answer
#              reasoned over, projected through ontology-labels.tsv so a raw
#              internal OntologyName (e.g. "caregiving_lexicon") never leaks —
#              e.g. "the Family Caregiving lexicon and U.S. Code Title 42".
#   {terms}    the surfaces the turn named but could not resolve to any loaded
#              concept — the same "asked but not loaded" set the abstention's
#              `unresolved` carries — e.g. "florb".
#   {citations} the documentary resources a recited definition was AUTHORED
#              from, read off the loaded lexicon's own `dcterms:source` edges —
#              e.g. "42 USC 300ii(7)". A DIFFERENT channel from {sources}: it
#              names where a gloss's wording came from, not what the engine
#              opened to answer, which is why the two are realized in separate
#              sentences and never joined into one list.
# The last two rows are NOT keyed by ResponseFrame. Definition provenance is a
# second, orthogonal channel about the same turn (any frame that recites a
# definition may carry it), so it gets its own row plus its own panel LABEL row
# — the label is loaded here rather than typed into a renderer, for the same
# reason every other surface is.
# Cite: Reiter & Dale (2000), realization + lexicalization stages; Reiter (1978)
# closed-world assumption (the honest boundary of the system's own knowledge).
